question: For already-visible English article prose, is optional on a late async face registration alone sufficient to preserve the reading point, or is early registration a necessary candidate?
sourceBaseline: 9ec879f3 accepted preview; extend_head/font tokens/typography immutable SHA captured; E13 WIP not built

variants.C: same @font-face optional registered in head before initial layout

controlledScope: One real public Noto Serif regular400 Latin WOFF2, all other Google faces withheld equally, article original real content/markup. Tests discovery timing, not full brand-font design or all-page remedy. Browser-only document/route overlay; no production edit.

cases.stimulus: face registered and ready before reading anchor is centered
stylesheet release after reader centered; font bytes immediately available from deterministic fixture
stylesheet release after reader centered; font bytes held another1200ms, exceeding optional short block period

decisionEvidence: Compare original marker docY/viewportY, rootY, document height and prose text range metrics before and after controlled registration+font readiness. Identical no-input anchor rect afterlate swap rejects instability hypothesis; B late reflow disproves URL optional alone; C stability supports early-registration candidate only under fixtures.
smallestFailure: No input/wheel/focus change, but original marker viewport or document coordinate changes >0.5CSSpx after font registration. Root scroll alone is insufficient due scroll anchoring.
checks: same original footnote node remains connected
visible original article text remains available throughout
timebox: 25min maximum; 3variants x3cases once; stop if font/fixture/trace invalid, retain failure; one browser sequential
outOfScope: font license redistribution; fetched binary fixture only in registered tmp
networkScope: Read-only local preview and exactly one Google Fonts CSS + chosen public WOFF2 download for deterministic fixture, bounded fetch. Stub GA scripts, block model/contact/subscription endpoints and other remote resource reads. No credentials or paid calls.
